F01.P1.justification: final int n = 7; return n; — standard immutable local binding.

F01.P2.fragment:
static long counter = 0;
static final long LIMIT = 100;
F01.P2.justification: static long counter = 0; static final long LIMIT = 100; at class/file scope.

F02.P1.justification: Java definite-assignment analysis permits declare-without-initializer then assign on both branches of an if/else, exactly the pattern required.

F02.P2.justification: Java arrays are always zero/default-initialized; no documented mechanism for genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. Named substitution per R9: byte[] b = new byte[16]; b[0]=1; return b[0];

F03.P2.justification: xs.set(1, 42); on a java.util.List (e.g. ArrayList) mutates in place through the existing name.

F04.P1.justification: Java has no documented mechanism for a second name to alias-and-write an existing local scalar variable's storage (no references/pointers/inout to locals); wrapping in a mutable object changes identity of what's aliased, not the local itself, and is excluded by the probe's own rubric elsewhere (F05.P2).

F04.P2.justification: List<Integer> window = Collections.unmodifiableList(xs); — documented non-copying read-only view; window.get(0) reads without copying elements.

F04.P3.justification: Reference identity via ==. Route `first` through a one-element List, retrieve as `second`, test `first == second` (documented reference-equality operator distinct from .equals()).

F05.P1.justification: Ordinary call f(x) on a List argument passes the reference by value; callee can read/write/resize elements of the same underlying object, observable through x afterward.

F05.P2.justification: Java has no documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar (primitive int) local variable; no ref/out/inout parameters, no address-of. The rubric explicitly disallows a mutable-container substitution as FULL for this probe.

F05.P3.justification: Function<Integer,Integer> neg = a -> k - a; (k captured, effectively final) then xs.stream().map(neg)... — lambda captures enclosing local and is passed by name to Stream.map.

F06.P1.justification: mid(List<Integer> xs){ return xs.get(1); } — returns an autoboxed Integer, a call-site binding, and return of y.

F06.P2.justification: record Pair(int q, int r) {} (Java 16+ record) used as the standard multiple-result mechanism; divmod2 returns new Pair(a/b, a%b).

F07.P1.justification: int r = a * b + c; ordinary precedence and operators.

F07.P2.justification: int q = a / b; int m = a % b; double d = (double) a / b; — Java int division truncates toward zero, % follows dividend sign, explicit cast for real division.

F08.P1.justification: int m = Integer.MAX_VALUE; int o = m + 1; — Java has no checked/wrapping/saturating standard arithmetic ops returning an optional; the plain + silently wraps (two's complement), which is the checked-mode-equivalent, deterministic, documented behavior for this recipe.

F08.P2.fragment:
int q = (b == 0) ? 0 : a / b;
return q;
F08.P2.justification: int q = (b == 0) ? 0 : a / b; — Java has no checked-division-to-optional standard op; explicit guard is the documented next rung.

F09.P1.justification: boolean eq = s1.equals(s2); — content comparison via String.equals.

F09.P2.justification: xs.sort(Comparator.reverseOrder()); boolean lt = a < b; — explicit descending order supplied, in-place sort of the List.

F10.P1.justification: int small; try { small = Math.toIntExact(big); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { small = 0; } — Math.toIntExact is the standard checked narrowing operation.

F10.P2.justification: double sum = i + d; — implicit widening of int to double at the + operator, no explicit conversion syntax needed or permitted.

F11.P1.justification: int e = xs.get(i); — ordinary indexed read on List, throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range i.

F11.P2.justification: List<Integer> part = xs.subList(1, 4); — documented view sharing backing storage with xs (not a copy).

F12.P1.justification: Optional<Integer> o = Optional.empty(); int n = o.orElse(0); — type-level optionality via java.util.Optional and its standard fallback operation.

F12.P2.justification: Function<Integer,Integer> h = a -> a + 1; Optional<Integer> p = o.map(h); int result = p.orElse(0); — Optional.map is the standard optional-aware chaining operation, no explicit if/switch.

F13.P1.fragment: static int parseTwice(String s) { return Integer.parseInt(s) * 2; }
F13.P1.justification: int parse_twice(String s) { return Integer.parseInt(s) * 2; } — Integer.parseInt throws unchecked NumberFormatException which propagates automatically without explicit handling.

F13.P2.justification: int n; try { n = Integer.parseInt(s); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { n = 0; } — standard local catch-based recovery.

F14.P1.justification: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rect {} ; record Circle(double r) implements Shape {} ; record Rect(double w, double h) implements Shape {} — sealed hierarchy is a closed alternative set enforced by the compiler (Java 17+ sealed classes).

F14.P2.justification: double area = switch (s) { case Circle c -> Math.PI * c.r() * c.r(); case Rect r -> r.w() * r.h(); }; — pattern-matching switch over a sealed hierarchy is checked exhaustively by the compiler with no default arm required (Java 21+).

F14.P3.justification: Plain (unsealed) interface Shapes.area() in unit `shapes`, implemented by Circle/Rect there and by Tri in a separate compilation unit, dispatched through the abstract type — uses the multi-unit javac recipe frozen in toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes.

F15.P1.justification: static <T> T head(List<T> xs) { return xs.get(0); } — declared result type T is statically recoverable from the generic signature even though erased at runtime; used at Integer and String call sites.

F15.P2.justification: static <T extends Comparable<T>> T max_of(T a, T b) { return a.compareTo(b) > 0 ? a : b; } — declaration-site bound via extends Comparable<T>.

F15.P3.justification: interface Named { String tag(); } with A, B implementing it; List<Named> items holding one of each; items.get(0).tag() dispatched at runtime to A's implementation.

F16.P1.justification: List<Integer> xs = new ArrayList<>(List.of(1,2,3)); int total = xs.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum(); — standard sum/stream operation.

F16.P2.justification: Map<String,Integer> mp = new HashMap<>(); mp.put("a",1); iterate mp.entrySet() to sum values; int miss = mp.getOrDefault("b", 0); — HashMap's unspecified iteration order and getOrDefault's documented absent-key fallback.

F17.P1.justification: try (FileReader r = new FileReader("data.txt")) { ... } — try-with-resources guarantees close() runs on every exit path including exceptions (AutoCloseable).

F17.P2.justification: Java has no deterministic end-of-lifetime hook (finalize() is deprecated/nondeterministic/removed in recent releases; Cleaner is GC-driven and nondeterministic). Nearest standard substitute per the probe's own named exception: an explicit close() invoked by a try-with-resources scoped construct, incrementing `released` deterministically exactly once at scope exit.

F18.P1.justification: System.out.println("x"); — java.lang is implicitly available with no import declaration required.

F18.P2.fragment:
class Util { public static int pubAdd(int a, int b) { return a + b + secret(); } private static int secret() { return 1; } }
int result = Util.pubAdd(2, 3);
F18.P2.justification: package util; class Util { public static int pub_add(int a,int b){ return a+b+secret(); } private static int secret(){ return 1; } } called from outside as Util.pub_add(2,3) — Java access modifiers (public/private) enforce the boundary; uses the multi-unit javac recipe.

F19.P1.justification: ExecutorService with two Callable<Integer> tasks (or two Thread instances) computing 20 and 22, Future.get() on both, sum = 42 — java.util.concurrent is the standard shipped concurrency facility.

F19.P2.justification: java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong counter; two threads each call counter.incrementAndGet() 1000 times; join both; counter.get() == 2000 — AtomicLong's read-modify-write is documented by the JDK as atomic/race-free.

F20.P1.justification: The Java Foreign Function & Memory API (java.lang.foreign) can declare and call C `abs(int)` using only the standard library, but on many currently-common JDK versions this requires an --enable-preview flag or is only fully finalized in the newest LTS (Java 22+); absent a confirmed toolchain fingerprint in this packet, this is recorded as requiring a flag/mode outside the strict frozen recipe.

F20.P2.justification: javac/java produces JVM bytecode (.class files), not a native compiled artifact with linker-visible symbols; there is no way to produce an nm-visible unmangled `add2` symbol under the frozen recipe.
